About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Growth Lead to build the growth engine for a new product line. Your mandate includes both acquiring customers that don’t use Ramp today, and driving adoption of the new product among existing customers. You’ll help shape how customers discover the product, understand its value, and decide to adopt it.

We are looking for someone who can determine which growth channels are most pertinent for their product, figure out the strategy for those channels and then successfully execute on the strategy. You’ll decide what to test, launch campaigns, and turn what works into repeatable growth. You should be equally comfortable developing a strategy, writing a landing page, digging into funnel performance, and building an automated workflow.

What You'll Do

  • Set the growth strategy and execute on it. Identify the audiences, messages, and channels with the greatest potential. Turn ideas into live experiments, and scale up the successful experiments into perpetual lead generators.

  • Acquire customers beyond Ramp’s existing base. Build campaigns that introduce the product to new businesses and convert interest into qualified pipeline. Develop a clear understanding of customer needs and translate it into compelling reasons to act.

  • Make the product part of the broader Ramp sale. Partner with sales to increase your product’s attach rate in deals that were initiated through other products. Improve the positioning, campaigns, and sales touchpoints that help customers understand where the product fits and why it matters.

  • Drive adoption across existing customers. Build cross-sell programs that drive adoption of the product among existing Ramp customers

  • Build and operate the channel mix. Launch and optimize landing pages, conversion funnels, paid search and social, SEO, sponsorships, direct mail, and events.

  • Use automation to multiply your impact. Create workflows that reduce manual work across campaign execution, experimentation, and reporting. Use AI thoughtfully to move faster without making every initiative dependent on additional resources.

What You Need

  • Minimum 2 years of experience in management consulting, investment banking, private equity, venture capital, and/or growth / operations at a fast-growing startup

  • Demonstrated ability to dissect complex problems, identify solutions, and drive these solutions to completion with a high degree of autonomy

  • Proficiency with data analytics with an ability to draw key insights from both quantitative and qualitative data

  • High level of resourcefulness and a track record of being a fast learner

  • Communication skills to influence others at all levels and across all functions within the organization to rally behind shared business goals

What Success Looks Like

You’ve built a clearer understanding of which audiences, messages, and channels drive growth for the product. Promising experiments have become repeatable programs. More new customers are discovering the product, and more existing Ramp customers are adopting it.

You should also build a way of working that gets faster and smarter with each experiment, not a collection of campaigns that depend on constant manual effort. Thinking from first principles should lead you to discover growth tactics that are new to the company.

Who We Are:

Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.

The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.

What We Value:

We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

  • Seek Excellence.
  • Be Selective To Be Effective.
  • Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
  • Disagree Transparently.
  • Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
  • Build Dream Teams.

About the Galaxy Summer Internship Program

The Galaxy NYC Summer Internship Program is an immersive, nine-week experience taking place on-site in our New York HQ office. During the nine weeks, you will gain hands-on, practical work experience on our the FP&A Team, working on real products and problems alongside the people building them. In addition to learning on the job, Galaxy interns participate in professional development programming, social events, and networking opportunities with senior leaders.

The FP&A team coverage spans all Galaxy segments, including Global Markets, Asset Management & Digital Infrastructure, and Data Centers. We track how each desk is performing, figure out what’s driving the results, and turn the numbers into clear takeaways for business leaders and senior management. As our FP&A intern, you’ll work with the team to analyze the drivers of business performance. You’ll look for trends, explain what’s moving the P&L (profit and loss) and help build the reports and dashboards leadership uses. You’ll learn about a diverse business and how to explain the story behind the numbers.

Program Dates: June 7th – August 6th, 2027

What You'll Do:

  • Performance analysis: Analyze business performance by month, quarter and year-to-date. Find the key trends and explain what’s behind them, such as client activity, product mix, or expense changes.
  • P&L driver analysis: Help review the daily and month-to-date P&L. Point out the biggest moves and link them to the products, clients, or crypto price changes behind them, such as BTC or ETH.
  • KPI trends: Track trading volumes, client activity and how revenue is split across products and regions. Point out what’s growing, what’s slowing and what stands out.
  • G&A expense process: Support the monthly G&A expense process by comparing actuals to budget and forecast, following up with cost owners on variances, and summarizing what’s driving changes in spend.

Product Marketing turns Chainalysis innovation into customer value. We position our intelligence as solutions customers can understand and consume through our platform, shape how we commercialize them, and give GTM the stories and strategic assets to win.

The public sector is a priority growth segment for Chainalysis, spanning law enforcement, intelligence agencies, regulators and tax authorities. As digital assets become more integrated into the financial system, these organizations need the intelligence, tools and tradecraft to advance their missions—from shaping policy and enforcing the rules to disrupting illicit networks and protecting national security. This role connects Chainalysis capabilities to those mission priorities, with a clear, compelling story for agency leaders and operational teams.

As Senior Product Marketing Manager for the Public Sector, you will own how Chainalysis shows up in the market for these buyers. You will shape our intelligence, data, products, AI capabilities, and services into a differentiated customer story—one that connects to real workflows, urgent problems, and mission outcomes.

This is a role for a strong marketer and an exceptional writer. You can take a complex capability, a shifting market, or a fuzzy customer problem and shape it into a sharp point of view, a persuasive narrative, and practical tools that sellers and customers actually use. You will work closely with Product, Sales, Marketing & Communications, subject-matter experts, and GTM Solutions & Readiness teams to make the story land in the market.

In this role, you’ll:

Position the value

  • Define and evolve the public sector value narrative: what Chainalysis enables, why it matters, and why we are meaningfully different.

  • Build messaging for priority buyer and user personas, from agency leaders to investigators, intelligence analysts, regulators and tax specialists.

  • Create the narratives, proof points, and strategic assets that help sellers communicate differentiated value with conviction.

  • Own public-sector competitive intelligence, translating market moves into clear offensive and defensive positioning for deal teams.

Turn value into solutions

  • Partner with Product, R&D, Marketing & Communications, and subject-matter experts to translate innovation into compelling industry solutions, use cases, and sales plays.

  • Lead go-to-market planning for launches, major releases, platform capabilities, and commercial offerings.

  • Shape customer-facing value narratives for pricing, packaging, and usage-based commercial models, including business cases, operational value and mission impact.

  • Bring a customer lens to product and market decisions: explain not only what a capability does, but how it advances the customer’s mission.

Win and learn in market

  • Produce the strategic content that moves government opportunities forward: first-call decks, solution briefs, talk tracks, discovery frameworks, proof points, and sales plays.

  • Partner with Product, Product Marketing, GTM & Enablement teams to scale the strongest narratives into field tools and enablement.

  • Bring customer, field, partner, and competitive insight back into the work — sharpening positioning, converting market evidence into credible stories, and building repeatable use cases.

We’re looking for candidates who have:

  • 5–8 years in product, solutions, industry, or B2B enterprise technology marketing, with experience marketing to public-sector customers across law enforcement, intelligence, regulatory or tax functions.

  • A demonstrated ability to build positioning and messaging that changes how customers and sellers see a problem—not simply content that fills a library.

  • Exceptional writing and editorial judgment. You can write crisp headlines, persuasive narratives, practical sales content, and executive-level messaging; you know the difference between jargon and precision.

  • Familiarity with investigative, intelligence, national-security, regulatory or tax use cases for intelligence and technology, and the policy developments shaping digital-asset markets.

You’ll thrive here if:

You can shape complexity into a story people remember and a sales conversation people can use. You write with precision, bring sound judgment to ambiguous problems, build for repeatability rather than one-off requests, and care about the quality of what reaches customers and the field.
